title: Value
definition: A value is a represented piece of information that a program can store, compare, transform, or communicate.
purpose: Give program data a precise unit of meaning that can be classified and processed.
history: Programming languages distinguish values from the source notations, storage locations, and encodings used to express them.
mental_model: A value is the information carried by a card; its type states which rules apply, while representation states how the information is encoded.
analogy: A labeled card carries information; the analogy fails because runtime values do not necessarily occupy one independent physical card or memory cell.
real_world_usage: Representing identifiers, quantities, flags, and missing information
common_mistakes: Confusing a value with its literal
Classifying by visual appearance instead of intended meaning
industry_notes: Data contracts should state the meaning, type, valid range, and absence policy of important values.
ai_notes: AI-proposed types must be checked against domain meaning and boundary examples.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to distinguish the number 42, the text value "42", and the source literal used to write each.
exercise_candidates: Classify visually similar values by meaning and type
lab_candidates: Build a value classification table for imported records
project_candidates: Define the data dictionary of a transformation console
